title: Rav Ukva of Mishan

paragraphs: [Shabbat 36b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.37b.6) mentions him telling Rav Ashi, “You who are close to Rav and Shmuel,” etc. At [43a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.43a.14),[^1]
he said to Rav Ashi, “This works for the summer months,” etc.[^2]
Hyman reports that [the Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Shabbat.3.1.2), at the supplied locator לג:, says the ruling follows Rav Ashi because he is the later authority.
Hyman says that apparently he too took part with Rav Ashi in arranging the Talmud.[^3]

notes.text: [Hyman’s print, vol. III, p. 979](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=146) gives 36b. The corresponding exchange is at the linked 37b, also cited by [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2863&lang=en). The Gemara describes the closeness in terms of the place where Rav and Shmuel lived.

The summer-months challenge begins at 43a and continues at [43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.43b.1). The linked Rosh quotes Ukva and says that Rav Ashi, the later authority, accepted his words. Hyman’s printed Rosh locator is לג:.
Hyman conjectures that Ukva participated in arranging the Talmud with Rav Ashi.
